policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 1:3 reads 'and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father' with no 'the Lord' before the name; the added κυρίου of r01 would have been rendered.

Pure Greek word order between καινὴν and γράφων σοι; ASV 'as though I wrote to thee a new commandment' translates either arrangement identically. The verse note is alternative_rendering (Cyria) and bears on the address, not this unit.
Word order only (ἡ ἐντολή ἐστιν / ἐστιν ἡ ἐντολή); ASV 'This is the commandment' renders both alike and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'many deceivers are gone forth into the world' renders ἐξῆλθον; r01 εἰσῆλθόν ('are entered into') is excluded by 'gone forth'.
ASV 'that ye lose not' is second person plural, matching ἀπολέσητε; r01 ἀπολέσωμεν would be 'we lose'. The 'Or, destroy' note is alternative_rendering of the same verb and does not bear on person.

ASV text reads 'the things which we have wrought' = εἰργασάμεθα. The mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read ye.' attaches to this unit (the other two verbs are already second person in every reading) and marks r01 εἰργάσασθε as the margin, confirming the base as the rendered text.
ASV 'but that ye receive a full reward' is second person plural, rendering ἀπολάβητε rather than r01 ἀπολάβωμεν ('we receive').

ASV 'Whosoever goeth onward' renders προάγων, and the mapped alternative_rendering note 'Or, taketh the lead' offers a second English sense of that same verb; r01 παραβαίνων ('transgresseth') fits neither text nor margin.
In the second clause ASV reads 'he that abideth in the teaching' with no qualifier; r01's added τοῦ Χριστοῦ would have given 'the teaching of Christ' as in the first clause.
Word order of the postpositive γὰρ with λέγων only; ASV 'for he that giveth him greeting' renders both readings identically.
ASV 'but I hope to come unto you' suits γενέσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς and ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς alike; English 'come unto you' does not distinguish the two infinitives and no note is mapped.
ASV 'that your joy may be made full' renders ὑμῶν; r01 ἡμῶν would be 'our joy'.
Word order of the periphrastic πεπληρωμένη ᾖ only; ASV 'may be made full' renders either arrangement.
ASV 1:13 ends 'salute thee' with no 'Amen'; r01's added Ἀμήν is unrendered.
